body.target_estimand: For the binary kernel, \(\tau_c(y)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a=1}^Kc_aY_i(a)\) on \(y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K}\). For a bounded schedule \(x\in[L,U]^{n\times K}\), the same causal contrast is \(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a=1}^Kc_ax_{i,a}\); on endpoint schedules \(x=L+(U-L)y\), zero sum gives the qualified identity \(n^{-1}\sum_{i,a}c_ax_{i,a}=(U-L)\tau_c(y)\).

sampling_model.design: Before outcomes are observed, the designer may choose any outcome-independent law on \(\mathcal A_K^n\), including arbitrary dependence and support on allocation faces. The attaining design assigns independently with \(q_a^\star=|c_a|/2\) on active arms and zero on inactive arms. For bounded outcomes, the implemented estimator is the conditional expectation of the normalized binary Airy rule, so the auxiliary Bernoulli variables are integrated out and assignment remains the only experimental randomness.
sampling_model.overlap: The unrestricted game imposes no overlap restriction. The proved all-count lower bound covers every realized count vector, including allocations entirely or partly to inactive arms and every face with zero count for one or more active arms.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no superpopulation nuisance estimation. The binary support-two case has one contrast-orthogonal coordinate; support at least three uses the finite response-alphabet dual score and every contrast-orthogonal tube direction. The bounded extension introduces no new nuisance model: it normalizes observed outcomes, Bernoulliizes them only inside a finite conditional expectation, and Rao--Blackwellizes to a total rule of the actual labeled bounded data.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 gives the unrestricted binary two-arm Airy expansion, while Theorem 2.3 gives the bounded two-arm endpoint reduction.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Theorem 1, the support-two reduction proposition, and Proposition prop:bounded-outcome-reduction

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 treats unrestricted bounded two-arm design and estimation by symmetrization and Bernoulliization.
Theorems 2.1--3.2 concern permutation symmetrization and minimax design within linear-estimator schemes.
The paper studies minimax precision and inference-constrained designs under a conditional-mean class rather than the fixed-schedule unrestricted nonlinear game.
Theorems 2 and 3 give sharp minimax results under unbiased estimation of bounded finite-population totals.
Second-order minimaxity can be characterized through a positive solution of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.
The paper develops conventional design-based estimators and variance adjustments for pairwise contrasts in multi-arm randomized trials.
The paper optimizes adaptive assignments for heteroscedastic Gaussian multi-arm shrinkage risk.

body.tldr: For every fixed \(K\ge2\) and every zero-sum, \(\ell^1\)-normalized contrast, the unrestricted binary finite-population game has risk \(R_n^{\{0,1\}}(c)=n^{-1}-C_AV_c(s_c/2)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\). For every fixed finite \(L<U\), the bounded-outcome game is exactly \(R_n^{[L,U]}(c)=(U-L)^2R_n^{\{0,1\}}(c)\). The same contrast-weighted independent assignment attains the scaled expansion with a total Rao--Blackwellized nonlinear Airy rule. The published two-arm binary and bounded results are the support-two anchors; the new geometry is the response-alphabet and all-allocation-face closure for contrasts with at least three active coordinates. Rational contrasts and rational endpoints admit terminating exact all-future certificates; rational bracketing transfers the mathematics, but not Turing evaluation, to unrepresented reals.

project_justification.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 3.1, supplies the unrestricted binary support-two Airy law, and its Theorem 2.3 supplies the bounded two-arm endpoint reduction. Hull (2026), Theorem 1, is another bounded two-arm anchor. These sources do not give the finite response-alphabet curvature, multidimensional nuisance tube, or design-uniform all-face lower bound for a fixed contrast with at least three active coordinates, nor an exact all-future certificate for that class.
project_justification.niche: The paper treats every fixed zero-sum, \(\ell^1\)-normalized contrast as one natural class and every fixed finite outcome interval by an exact endpoint reduction. Support two has coefficients \(+1\) and \(-1\), curvature one, and the published scalar law. Support at least three requires the response-alphabet gauge and a target direction plus \(\ker(c^\top)\) to control nuisance directions on every allocation face.
project_justification.fill: The binary kernel proves the coefficient \(C_AV_c(s_c/2)^{2/3}\), an attaining contrast-weighted independent design and total nonlinear estimator, and a matching finite-schedule Bayes lower bound uniformly over dependent outcome-independent assignments, inactive-arm allocations, and missing-active-arm faces. Conditional Bernoulliization and Rao--Blackwellization then prove the exact identity \(R_n^{[L,U]}=(U-L)^2R_n^{\{0,1\}}\), yielding the scaled bounded expansion under the same allocation. Exact rational scaling extends the all-future certificate to rational endpoints.

body.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 3.1, is the unrestricted binary two-arm Airy benchmark, while Theorem 2.3 is the bounded two-arm endpoint-reduction anchor. Hull (2026), Theorem 1, also treats bounded outcomes in the two-arm unrestricted problem. The present support-two proposition recovers the binary coefficient even with additional inactive labels, and the exact bounded-outcome proposition extends endpoint reduction to every fixed contrast; the main new geometry remains the response-alphabet curvature and design-uniform all-face closure for support at least three. Bai (2023) treats symmetrization and linear-estimator design, Kallus (2021) a different conditional-mean minimax-variance objective, and Aronow and Lopatto (2026) unbiased estimation. Levit (1986) supplies the positive-eigenfunction architecture. Schochet (2018) develops conventional multi-arm design-based estimators, Rosenman and Hunter (2026) a different adaptive Gaussian shrinkage problem, and Hammer et al. (1996) the four-regimen application rather than a theorem comparator.
body.interpretation: The coefficient separates a universal one-dimensional Airy phenomenon from finite response-alphabet geometry. Support two has curvature one; with at least three active coefficients, \(V_c(s_c/2)\) is the exact binary-response cost of the target direction. Bounded outcomes add only the squared physical scale \((U-L)^2\): endpoint schedules certify the lower inequality, while conditional Bernoulliization and Rao--Blackwellization certify the upper inequality without changing the assignment. Thus correlation, inactive-arm allocation, and zero-count faces cannot improve the second-order coefficient on either response scale.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The expansion is pointwise for each fixed arm count, fixed contrast, and fixed finite endpoint interval. Remainder constants may deteriorate when an active contrast weight approaches zero, so there is no growing-\(K\) or vanishing-weight uniformity. The bounded reduction does not cover unbounded outcomes or outcome-dependent designs. Exact evaluators require rationally represented contrasts and rational endpoints; continuity and exact scaling give mathematical extensions to real inputs but no algorithm for an unrepresented real number.
body.honest_scope: The binary theorem covers every fixed \(K\ge2\), zero-sum, \(\ell^1\)-normalized contrast over fixed binary schedules. The exact reduction extends its risk and scaled Airy expansion to every fixed bounded schedule in \([L,U]^{n\times K}\) for finite real \(L<U\). The published two-arm binary law and bounded Theorem 2.3 are anchors; the new content is the support-at-least-three response-alphabet closure, uniform control of all allocation faces, and exact rational all-future certification. Designs may be arbitrarily dependent but must be selected without the schedule, and estimators may be randomized full-label kernels; the attaining bounded rule integrates out its auxiliary Bernoulliization. The paper makes no claim for growing arm counts, vanishing-weight uniformity, unbounded outcomes, outcome-dependent assignment, weak-null inference, or covariate balancing. Certificates are exact for rational contrasts and rational endpoints only, while the coefficient extends mathematically to real inputs without a Turing-evaluator claim.
